questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to travel to a destination I have never visited before

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. My host university was very good at sending out info mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information mails and information meetings

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. I was in Edinburgh, and I ended up renting an appartment with a friend through Platform_, which was expensive, but overall super great and worth all the money.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start searching in good time!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got an email saying where and when we needed to go, and when we arrived, there was big signs indicating what to do. The process was quick, and the staff was great and worked very fast.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of signs and a lot of staff to help out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: First I did not get the courses that I wanted, so I applied for a course change, and then I was lucky and got all of my priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep track of your inbox. All important info should arrive to you there:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose two third-year courses and one second-year course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked the UCPH teaching style better. At my host university sometimes the lectures was very hectic since there were so many people in one room at a time, and sometimes people needed to leve before the lecture ended, to make it to another lecture on time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Social Life and Climate Change 
- Anthropology of Health and Healing
- Ritual and Religion

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend "Anthropology of Health and Healing", since it's a very interesting course, providing you with a lot of very interesting readings and theories, to draw on in your future work.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Council tax - Apparently you get asked to pay council tax in Edinburgh, but full time student should not pay that, and you can ask for a refund.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation - You can pay every month or you can pay for the whole period.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was A LOT of different societies with a lot of different sports and social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join as many communities as your social battery allows. it's a great way to meet people and new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to destinations within your country that you would like to see/experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it did not feel like there was a local culture at my uni, since there were so many exchange students from all over the world

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask where the local student go, and ask if you can join some time

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural difference challenging, since it was not that different from home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How people randomly initiated conversations with strangers. It was so nice to experience strangers complimenting one another and small-talking at cafés. That was very different from what I am use to in Copenhagen where people certainly do not talk to each other, and definetly not to strangers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: - Say hi and initiate conversations/ask questions to students every day! Great way to meet friends and I felt like people really appreciated it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy a bus card - you will need it more than you think.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing uni life in another country was amazing, but for me, the most rewarding experience was creating a life for my self outside of the university as well.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To figure out where to locals go.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
